D.t: Cory Booker leads by 26.2 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 935,857 votes; a one point swing is about 17,860 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +17.1 and D +35.6. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Essex, a projected net 183,394 votes; Hudson, a projected net 115,031 votes; Bergen, a projected net 102,847 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Monmouth, D +9.7, 8.0% of the vote; Gloucester, D +9.4, 3.7% of the vote; Sussex, R +8.7, 1.8% of the vote; Hunterdon, D +9.1, 1.8% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Cory Booker runs furthest behind in Burlington, Gloucester, Mercer. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 69% of voters, 56 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.43 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 57% of voters, 61 to 36, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.83 points; Men, 46% of voters, 57 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.29 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Cory Booker: Immigration voters 29 to 69, Midsize counties 51 to 46, White voters 56 to 42. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
